title: Patriots placing A.J. Brown on IR with high ankle sprain: Source
content:
The New England Patriots will be without their top playmaker for at least four games.

The team plans to place star wide receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve due to a high ankle sprain suffered in Wednesday’s season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks, a team source tells The Athletic.

Brown is eligible to return to the field for the Patriots’ Week 6 game against the New York Jets.

It’s a big blow to a Patriots offense that was supposed to be among the best in the league. They gave up a first-round pick to acquire Brown in hopes he would bring out the best in quarterback Drake Maye. Now, an offense that struggled against Seattle faces at least four games without Brown.

Following the August trade of Kayshon Boutte, 2025 third-round pick Kyle Williams is the Patriots’ top backup behind Brown. But he struggled as a rookie and has so far made strides only in running straight-line go routes with concerns remaining on his abilities in other phases of the passing game. Still, coaches have lauded the work Williams has done behind the scenes and now need to lean on the Washington State product more than expected.

It also creates a tougher challenge for Maye, who is coming off arguably the worst game of his career and faces lingering questions after a four-game slump in last season’s playoffs.

The schedule isn’t easy either. The Patriots host the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2 before heading on the road for games against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills.

And now they know they’ll be without their top wide receiver.
